summary: Part 3 of the Nike deep dive (published 2026-09-20) focuses on management's 'decisive action' across the supply chain — cutting costs, streamlining operations, and right-sizing distribution to match weak demand, which he reads as an admission that demand looks poor. He describes the consumer backdrop: tariffs, wars, oil prices, inflation, and AI job-loss fears make consumers pull back on $200–300 discretionary sneakers. The China situation is especially bleak: Nike reiterates commitment to the market and teams there are executing a 'comprehensive reset,' but they haven't even found the right strategy yet, so Greater China will remain a headwind for a long time. Product-specific headwinds compound this: sportswear and Jordan streetwear are expected to stay negative for the fiscal year as consumers are tired of Jordan retro re-releases (shelves at Foot Locker still carry unsold Jordans, once scarcity-driven). Nike plans 12+ new footwear styles with distinct consumer journeys, though payoff timing is uncertain. He agrees management is adjusting prudently to a hand it can't control. Call: NKE UNCERTAIN.
